transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-03-28
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Ariel Park (Redwood AE), Samir Kapoor (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (CTO, StratoWave), Luis Ortega (ML Eng), Priya Nair (SecOps)

00:00 Ariel (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Ariel from Redwood, with Samir our SE. quick intro — we'll do a discovery on model selection and deployment options, hosted vs dedicated vs private. Maya, do you want to kick off with your goals?
00:23 Maya (StratoWave): Sure, yeah, thanks Ariel. We're building a multilingual customer support assistant plus some doc retrieval + tool calls to our order system. Main things are context length — we have long conversations and docs — so 32k or 128k is interesting — and also tool-calling for actions like refund, order status.
00:45 Luis (StratoWave): Also want to know how open models compare on hallucination and latency; we prototype with Llama2 and Mistral but haven't benchmarked at scale.
01:10 Samir (Redwood SE): Great context. Quick normalization on terms — when we say "tool-calling" we mean function or external API invocation with structured outputs, and KV caching/prefix caching to keep latency down while serving longer contexts. Some transcribe quirks — sorry if I say "KV cash" a couple times, ha.
01:32 Ariel: Quick agenda: understand success criteria, constraints (security, residency), workload shape (tokens/sec, concurrency), model preferences (open vs closed), and then propose next steps/POC.
02:05 Maya: Success criteria — avg response latency < 600ms for short queries, <1.5s for retrieval-augmented answers; cost per user should be predictable; must support English + Spanish + Portuguese; SOC2 required and SSO via SAML. Private deployment is on the table if needed for compliance.
02:40 Priya (SecOps): To add, we need audit logs, KMS integration for customer keys, and VPC peering to our AWS account; if you offer on-prem we can consider but prefer Redwood Dedicated in our cloud first.
03:05 Samir: Helpful. On model side: open models we commonly recommend depending on tradeoffs — Mistral-Instruct / Mistral-large (good instruction following, cheaper tokens), Llama 3 variants, and some 70B open models. For long context we can use models quantized to 8-bit and still hit 32k and 128k variants — but there's latency cost with longer KV material.
03:40 Luis: Can Redwood host 128k context models in Dedicated? I heard memory constraints + cost skyrockets.
04:00 Samir: Yes, Dedicated can be provisioned with GPUs and memory to support 128k contexts — it's about the model variant and tokenization. We do kernel selection and memory mapping to keep KV cache efficient. Tradeoff: higher reserved cost but predictable throughput and lower tail latency than hosted fallback to smaller models.
04:35 Ariel: For a quick comparison: Hosted is fastest to start, pay-as-you-go; Dedicated is reserved capacity for predictability and throughput; Private (VPC/on-prem) gives network isolation + KMS control. Many teams start hosted for experimentation then move to Dedicated for production SLOs.
05:10 Maya: Regarding multilingual — which open models have best out-of-the-box Spanish/Portuguese? We tried Llama2 but quality was inconsistent.
05:30 Samir: Mistral-Instruct and some Llama 3 instruction-tuned variants show strong multilingual capability; we also do model selection with evaluation prompts early in POC — we can run your sample prompts across 3 model candidates and show quality/latency/cost tradeoffs.
06:05 Luis: Great. On hallucination — we're doing retrieval augmented generation (RAG) against our internal docs, so the model needs strong grounding and tool-calling to pull exact order info. How do you support deterministic tool outputs?
06:30 Samir: We recommend function calling patterns plus structured output schemas; Redwood runtime enforces output formats when possible and we support reranking/verification steps. For RAG, our prefix cache + chunking and vector store pairing reduces hallucination. We can add an LLM-based verifier step in the pipeline in POC.
07:05 Priya: Security question — is audit logging available at token or request level? And how are keys managed?
07:25 Ariel: Audit logs are available as part of Console; Dedicated and Private give more retention options. KMS integrations available with AWS KMS and HSM for Private. We'll share SOC2 and network docs in the follow-up.
08:00 Maya: Timeline — we'd like to do a 2-week POC with 3 model variants, one optimized for latency (smaller model, ~8k), one for quality at 32k, and one for 128k to test long doc flows. We want to run our prompt set and measure latency/cost/accuracy.
08:25 Samir: That's doable. For the 128k test we usually provision a temporary dedicated pool so you get consistent performance; that will let you see throughput instead of noisy hosted bursts.
09:00 Luis: Do you support streaming responses with function calls mid-stream? We want partial token responses while the tool call is pending.
09:18 Samir: We do streaming and function calling; caveat — streaming with complex tool workflows may require orchestration client-side. We can show sample patterns. There may be slight differences in SDKs between Hosted and Dedicated control plane but functionally similar.
10:00 Maya: Any existing customers with similar stacks who did multilingual + tool calling?
10:12 Ariel: Yes, a retail customer used a 32k Mistral variant + dedicated pool and reduced per-ticket handling latency by 45% and cost by ~30% after batching and prefix cache tuning — we can share an anonymized case study.
10:45 Priya: On compliance, if we choose Dedicated but keep data in Redwood-managed infra, is there encryption at rest with customer keys?
10:55 Ariel: Yes — Dedicated supports CMKs via AWS KMS; Private allows full customer-managed KMS/HSM and air-gapped if needed. We'll send the security doc.
11:30 Luis: For benchmarks, what metrics should we capture? I'm thinking p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, and hallucination rate on our eval set.
11:48 Samir: Exactly. We'll add throughput under target concurrency (you said ~20 concurrent users?), p95 and p99 latencies, and memory footprints. We'll also show batching impact and quantization tradeoffs.
12:20 Maya: Our concurrency will vary — baseline 10-20 concurrent, spike to 80 during business hours. Autoscaling/burst capacity is important.
12:40 Samir: Dedicated autoscaling policies + burst to hosted are possible if you want both predictability and spillover. But that gets into routing policies; we can recommend configs.
13:15 Priya: Network — we prefer VPC peering and no public egress for requests. Can Dedicated be peered?
13:28 Ariel: Yes, Dedicated supports VPC peering and private endpoints; Private gives you full private control plane too. We'll note that in the follow-up.
14:05 Luis: On model licensing — any restrictions on open models for commercial use?
14:15 Samir: Depends on the upstream model license, but for the open-source models we typically surface we’ve vetted permissive licenses; we can include license notes in the model catalog we send.
14:40 Maya: What about quantization — we heard 4-bit quantization can significantly reduce cost but may hurt quality. What's Redwood's position?
14:55 Samir: We recommend mixed profiles: 8-bit for most production to keep determinism, 4-bit for aggressive cost-savings where quality drop is acceptable. We'll include recommended quantization profiles per model variant.
15:30 Ariel: Recap and next steps — we'll send: pricing sheet, SOC2/network/KMS docs, benchmark template, and proposed POC plan for week of 4/5. Samir will run a quick internal bench and share candidate models (8k, 32k, 128k). Priya will send security questionnaire and VPC diagram.
16:05 Maya: Sounds good. Any blockers from Redwood side?
16:12 Samir: Nothing major; we'll need sample prompts and a small dataset for eval. Also confirm expected concurrency and a target SLO for the POC.
16:35 Ariel: I'll follow up with calendar invite for POC kickoff and include the checklist.
16:50 Maya: Thanks everyone, appreciate the clear plan.
17:00 End meeting

Notes: transcript contains occasional recognition errors (e.g., "KV cash"), some overlapping talk captured as short crosstalk lines. Links shared during call: [pricing-sheet.pdf] (we will attach in follow up), [SOC2-summary.pdf], [benchmark-template.xlsx].
